title: Observation in daily life
opening: Observation can happen while you are already doing something. In the message example, the words on screen are one thing; a guess about why the person wrote them is another. Noticing the difference may help you decide what to do next, but it does not tell you whether you agree.

modes.label: Notice a glimpse
modes.description: Notice a brief moment when you are already aware of what is happening during an ordinary activity.

modes.label: Return at transitions
modes.description: Use an everyday change, such as finishing one activity or entering a room, as another cue to notice what is already happening.

modes.label: Stay with the activity
modes.description: Stay with an activity’s experience a little longer. When attention wanders, return to what you are doing.

modes.label: Notice during challenge
modes.description: You can notice what is happening during a difficult moment too; you do not have to be calm first.

modes.label: Shift between particular and open attention
modes.description: Move attention between one detail, such as the message words, and the wider experience. Each view can show something different.

modes.label: Act, then notice the result
modes.description: Let what you notice inform an action, then notice what happened afterward. No particular result is required.

modeNote: These six ways can overlap and recur. Choose any one that fits; they are not a required order, and calm is not a prerequisite.

example.message: Can you send the current draft by three?
example.reply: Yes, I can send it by 2:30.

labels.example: A message and a possible assumption
labels.inspectExample: Show the message and possible assumption

ownPursuit.prompt: Choose a safe transition in your own pursuit, such as finishing one activity before starting another. Keep taking part; notice what is happening and use any mode that fits. The modes can overlap and recur.
ownPursuit.prediction: Before the transition, what, if anything, do you expect to notice about the activity or surroundings? What might you notice within yourself, if anything? A particular feeling or state is not required.
ownPursuit.observation: What actually happened around you? What, if anything, did you notice in your body, thoughts or feelings? Separate what happened from your explanation of why.
ownPursuit.revision: Did anything you noticed change what you did next or clarify what was happening? What did you notice afterward, if anything? It is fine if none of the modes seemed useful.

accessibility.modes: Choose any of six connected ways to notice. They can overlap and recur; the selected view is not progress or a required step.
accessibility.example: The message words, an assumption that is not stated, and one authored reply are separately labeled. The reply is an example, not the only valid response.
accessibility.ownPursuit: Write and save a private, unscored reflection about what you actually noticed in a safe transition in your own pursuit.
